observations: Both mirrors use a logical-name lease under the existing app-owned parent and retain the inner lock for intact legacy interop.
Supported replacement and open contend on the same lease. An independent workspace opened and wrote while the first still held its lease.

Late external displacement can commit on the already open inode, then fences the writer. The replacement directory is untouched and descriptor-relative cleanup removes the old temporary even on abort.
An older binary can acquire a displaced inner inode. The lease namespace must remain stable through coordinated leaf operations.
The offline app has no account cleanup caller. The coordination API adds no deletion operation.
